description.value: Knotted cord worked into the hauling harness, in which the turn direction, knot type and spacing record a route, a load and an outstanding obligation. A cord is an account and not a message: it has no tense, no way of stating anything that has been settled, and no means of referring to a person who owes nothing. Lodges read each other's cords on meeting and this is how a route is claimed, transferred or given up, so the object is the transaction rather than a report of it. The first mistake is to treat a cord as writing and ask for a translation, which produces a list of numbers and an increasingly patient hauler.

sampleGloss.value: two long turns, a reversed knot, then four short turns. Element by element: coldward route, owed back, four loads. Freely: on the coldward route, four loads still owing.

note.value: Recorded during elicitation and kept as the reference sample for this system.

notes.value: A sample recording of this system is eleven minutes of a hut with somebody's hands in it, and is retained because the register requires a recording of every entry.
